measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_grenade.mdl, models/w_satchel.mdl, models/w_357.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked A, D, D, D where the asset was B, D, A, B: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: Against the brief (a pistol lying on its side), the top, below and back-left views read as a pistol: a long slide, a grip at one end, a muzzle. The outline is still off. The grip is a tall, blocky box that reaches well past the slide's line, and the slide is a plain slab with no clear trigger guard. In sides.png the front and back views look more like a box than a pistol profile.

M2.reason: Measured size [7.8, 1.4, 9.6] against 'about 10 long': the length is 3.5% off (sizeOff 0.035), within the 15% band. The thin 1.4 dimension is vertical, which fits a pistol lying on its side.

M3.reason: Parts the brief implies, listed down to the small: slide, barrel and muzzle, grip (the magazine housing), trigger guard, trigger, front sight, rear sight, hammer. The slide, grip and muzzle are there. A trigger guard shows only as a small hook in the below view and is not clear. The sights are at most small nubs at the ends of the slide in sides.png, and the trigger and hammer are not distinct. A missing small part caps M3 at 1.

M4.reason: The brief asks for black and grey polymer and steel. The slide is grey steel and the grip is black, as in the sides and first-person views. The first-person slide is a little lighter and flatter than the game's gunmetal, but within what one would call the same grey.

M5.reason: The brief names no markings, but a standard sidearm would carry slide serrations and sight lines. In first-person.png the slide is a smeared, low-resolution grey with none of the game's crisp edges, and the grip's ribbed face in the top view is blocky. The detail is softer than the game's own guns at this size.

M6.reason: Measured by the line-up test, as directed. The asset (A, B, A, B positions across the four runs) was picked as the non-Valve model in one of four runs (the run where it stood at D), so three of four readings passed it. The directive caps M6 at 2 here.

M7.reason: The weapon lies on its side as the brief asks: the slide runs flat along the floor in the top and front views, the thin 1.4 dimension is vertical, and the grip points sideways. The muzzle end is at the front, and the first-person view places it upright in the hand.

M8.reason: Triangles are 78, under the Half-Life median of 142 and well under twice it, so the count passes. The check passes with no errors. But in the top, below and back-left views the grip reads as an open-topped box with a black inside and grey walls, and the muzzle is black. A player can see those openings, so 'nothing open' is not met.

W1.reason: In first-person.png the asset sits where the game's gun sits: the same horizontal place, the muzzle up and to the left, the grip under the hand, the same way round. In attack.png, the weapon keeps the same offset in the frame across all 14 shoot frames (about 138 to 140 px in each tile) with the hand beneath it, and it does not part from the hand.
